clinicalPearls: Suspected in patients with recurrent biliary-type or pancreatic-type pain, often after cholecystectomy, without an identifiable structural cause
Results from disordered motility or stenosis of the sphincter of Oddi, impairing biliary and pancreatic outflow
The modern classification distinguishes patients with objective abnormalities (raised liver or pancreatic enzymes, duct dilatation) from those with pain alone
Sphincter of Oddi manometry can demonstrate elevated basal sphincter pressure but is invasive and carries a significant risk of post-procedure pancreatitis
Randomised evidence has tempered enthusiasm for endoscopic sphincterotomy in pain-only presentations, where benefit is uncertain
Careful patient selection is essential because intervention carries real procedural risk with limited benefit in some subgroups
It should remain a diagnosis of exclusion after structural, biliary, and pancreatic pathology have been ruled out
reference.pathophysiology: Sphincter of Oddi dysfunction encompasses abnormal contractility or fixed narrowing of the muscular sphincter that governs flow of bile and pancreatic juice into the duodenum. Elevated sphincter tone, paradoxical contractions, or true papillary stenosis raise ductal pressure, producing biliary or pancreatic-type pain and, in some patients, transient enzyme elevation, duct dilatation, or recurrent pancreatitis. The disorder overlaps with functional gut-brain disorders and visceral hypersensitivity, which contributes to the ongoing controversy over how reliably manometry identifies patients who benefit from sphincter ablation.
additionalDifferentials: Retained or recurrent bile duct stones
Functional biliary or pancreatic pain without sphincter pathology
additionalInvestigations: Liver function tests and pancreatic enzymes captured during or shortly after pain episodes
Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography to exclude stones and structural disease
Endoscopic ultrasound to assess the distal duct and ampulla
Sphincter of Oddi manometry in carefully selected patients despite its risk
Cross-sectional imaging to evaluate the pancreas and biliary tree
redFlags: Jaundice, cholangitis, or markedly abnormal liver tests suggesting obstruction or stones
Recurrent acute pancreatitis requiring structural evaluation
Weight loss or a mass raising concern for ampullary or pancreatic malignancy
Development of post-procedure pancreatitis after intervention
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends on the subtype: patients with objective obstructive findings may benefit from sphincterotomy, whereas those with pain alone often gain little and remain at risk of procedural complications, so expectations must be set carefully.
pitfalls: Proceeding to sphincterotomy in pain-only patients despite weak evidence of benefit
Underestimating the substantial risk of post-ERCP pancreatitis from manometry and intervention
Failing to exclude retained stones and structural disease first
Overlooking a functional gut-brain disorder or visceral hypersensitivity as the true driver of pain
references: Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
Rome Foundation criteria for functional gallbladder and sphincter of Oddi disorders
management: Careful subtype classification, distinguishing patients with objective obstructive findings from those with pain alone before any intervention
Endoscopic biliary sphincterotomy for patients with objective enzyme or duct abnormalities most likely to benefit
Avoid sphincterotomy in pain-only presentations, where randomised evidence shows little benefit against real procedural risk
Trial of medical therapy such as antispasmodics (calcium channel blockers, nitrates) and neuromodulators such as tricyclic antidepressants for pain
Sphincter of Oddi manometry only in carefully selected patients, accepting the risk of post-procedure pancreatitis
Post-ERCP pancreatitis prophylaxis with rectal NSAIDs and pancreatic duct stenting when intervention is undertaken
Manage as a functional gut-brain disorder with realistic expectation-setting and multidisciplinary support
